title: Think on Me, Lord, for Thou Art Kind
description: Think on Me, Lord, for Thou Art Kind in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the East (Paisley, in print by 1911).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Think on me, Lord, for Thou art kind, And I am nee-dy, poor, and blind, And let the gifts Thou hast in store, En-rich me dail-y, more and more.

lines: Think on me, Lord, for Thou art kind,
And I am needy, poor, and blind,
And let the gifts Thou hast in store,
Enrich me daily, more and more.
I have no food my soul to feed,
Be Thou my Bread of Life indeed;
My parchèd spirit sighs, O give
The stream of Life that I may live.
My filthy raiment I disown,
Clothe with Thy righteousness alone,
And I shall walk approved by Thee,
Clad in Thy robe of purity.
I have no strength; in evil hour
I fall beneath temptation's power;
Be Thou my strength, and I shall stand
Upheld by Thine outstretched hand.
I cannot see the path to tread,
And blindly by my sins am led;
Come to my blindness, give me sight
That I may shape my course aright.
I cannot live if Thou deny
The prayer uplifted with my cry;
I cannot die, — in mercy give
Thy grace, that I may die or live.
Think on me, Lord, for Thou art kind,
And I am needy, poor, and blind;
And let the gifts Thou hast in store,
Enrich me daily, more and more.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the East (by 1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the East; set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
